summary: # Marvelous Designer 9 Shanghai Launch Event - Real-time Character Creation ## Introduction Thank you for inviting me to the new version of Marvelous Designer's new function launch after last year. First of all, I would like to introduce the content of the character's injury and how to make a reference. I will also cover how to use multi-channel textures and Substance Painter for texturing, as well as how to create costumes using Marvelous Designer and how to make a hair card using Ornatrix Hair. ## Overview of Marvelous Designer's New Functions Now, I would like to introduce the content of the next version of Marvelous Designer's new function launch. This includes how to use multi-channel textures and Substance Painter for texturing. I will introduce you to the workflow of creating a real-time character. ### Final Image Preview This is the final image of what I am going to introduce to you today. It looks very natural, doesn't it? Actually, I didn't model it. I just used the smartphone app, FaceApp, to make it fun. What do you think about it? ### Inspiration and Character Background Last time, I made a David Candy, and I applied FaceApp to it. In the early 1980s, I made a Japanese animation called Katchaman, which was released under the name of the bookworm. When I was young, I had a lot of fun watching it. Among the five characters, there is a character called Jun the Swan, who represents a white swan. I started thinking about what it would look like if I made a real-time movie about this character. ### Character Development In this animation, there are five hero characters. The third character is called Jun the Swan. She is the symbol of the white swan and is the only female character in the combination. I've been thinking about what it would look like if I put this character in the movie, so I started creating this. As you can see, I rode a motorcycle and I used a mobile phone like Yoyo. I wore a unique helmet, a pink suit, and a feather-shaped cape. I wore a chemical-based hat, comfort armor, and defense armor. ### Character Design Process I have been working on this character since I was 16 years old. If you wear normal clothes, you may be able to show the characteristics of the swan better. Even if many people can't tell that this is a swan, it doesn't matter. As long as you can bring some good memories to some people, that's enough. ### Facial Modeling and References The basic face and styling are decided by the early and middle-aged women in their 20s in Korea. The style is similar to that of a popular Korean vocalist. I tried to make a lot of references that are similar to the feeling I think. I didn't create a style that makes a certain character look like him; rather, I tried to make a face that is not in the world while thinking about the image of the swan. It is necessary to do facial modeling first. The reference was created for 3D scan images. I was curious about the shape of the face when I scanned a real person. I modeled the face freely with ZBrush Dynamesh and Sculptris, always paying attention not to deviate from the age of the swan and the appearance I had designed. ### Topology and UV Mapping I used ZBrush's G-LAP to achieve a well-organized topology. As you can see, I wrapped the low-polygon mesh with the new high-polygon mesh. The left image is a dynamic wire, and the middle image is a wrapping of the existing low-poly bond. I used two types of UV for unraveling the topology, focusing on maximizing the UV area of the face for better resolution. I divided the UV area into the face and neck, and used the Re-Zone UV for better mapping. For texturing, I used the multi-channel face from TEXTURING XYZ, which you can purchase on their website. You can download three texture sources: Albedo MAP, Displacement MAP, and Utility MAP. ### Texture Details The Albedo MAP has sliced spherical deformations for skin detail. The utility MAP contains a hemoglobin map that shows all kinds of blood in the RGB channel, along with a melanin map and a specular map. After purchasing the material, you can download these three questionnaires. To help you understand better, I will show you a video demonstrating how I used the G-texture transfer to create the mesh texture of the plan. Even if the inner part of the mouth or the nostrils is not perfect, you can edit it appropriately and use it. You can output up to 8K, and with the extra plate function, you can fill in the empty space outside the UV. ### Makeup Process As a man, I have entered a new field of makeup. I have seen eye shadow, eye line, and references. I have seen pure straight eyebrows and eye lines. I use a lot of eye shadows such as orange, grapefruit, and pink. The most difficult thing for me is that I can't tell what kind of lip color is good. In order to brighten my skin tone, I applied a layer mask to the utility map channel in Photoshop to adjust the color. I applied eye shadow, eye line, cheek touch, eyebrow line, lip tint, blemish remover, and dot makeup. To make your skin darker, I used the utility map channel's blood-red and black color pictures to apply them to the layers of the skin. Finally, I did eye shadow, eye line, blush, hairline, eyebrows, lipstick, and removed the flaws. ### Costume Creation Process Before I made the costume, I created the body first. I collected reference pictures to study the proportions and volume. Now, I'm going to start making the costume. The main colors are white, black, and gold, with a blue jacket as the top. I usually buy clothes from the MD store or download costume paper to customize them. I changed the size of the body to fit the body shape and combined small patterns to work with hyper-remote detail. I created a pose using the Transpose Master in the studio, combining the soft with one and making a layer to mask the joints. ### Animation and Exporting I used ZBrush for export and 3D Max for import, applying morph after including the T-Pose Mesh and the Pose Mesh. In Marvelous Designer animation mode, the pre-prepared Alambic file will be inserted, and the clothes will get the same animation effect as the pose. ### Hyper-Realistic Sculpting For the hyper-realistic sculpting work, we plan to rematch the costume mesh with the pose mesh and the unfolded pattern mesh, and export them to OBJ without welding. We imported two OBJ files to 3D Max and applied morph to them. ### Final Mesh and Details We added creases and details to the edges, and the final base mesh has been completed. The pattern element remains the same, and we added thickness and detailed modeling. ### Hair Creation Process Before I make the hair card mesh, I will put the reference hair mesh into ZBrush and make it simple using DynaMesh. I will use Ornatrix to create the hair card mesh, which is convenient because the Unwrap is automatically organized into a square. ### Eyebrow and Hair Texture In order to make the eyebrows, I gathered some references for the direction of the texture. I checked the shape of the eyebrows first, then made the card mesh as I did for the hair. I focused on the direction of the eyebrows using the ZBrush Fiber Mesh, which allows me to create beautiful shapes. ### Lighting and Final Rendering To achieve the desired look, I made several combinations of lighting and background colors, ultimately choosing TAMOS color for the background. I set up the lighting for key light, rim light, and fill light using three-point lighting, which helps express the good choreography. ### Conclusion This is the final finished image. You can find more information through our radio station and our YouTube channel. Thank you for joining me today!
